A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 36-page SCAM time-series forecasting paper, including Appendices A–H and the checklist. Text and rendered-image comparisons establish that pages 2–36 are identical; differences on page 1 are confined to author-affiliation markers and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting experiments, component ablations, and synthetic and real-data analyses in Section 4 and the appendices. Appendix H includes the authors' experimental results and baseline reruns.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original forecasting experiments, ablations, and analyses in Section 4 and the appendices, including the authors' results in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The reconstruction network, adaptive masked co-training objective, selective spectral norm regularization, and predictor-only inference remain identical in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four ETT datasets, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, four PeMS datasets, and synthetic noisy-sinusoid case. No evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MLP, CycleNet, PatchTST, and iTransformer (ITRANS). The distinction between published baseline scores and the authors' reruns is unchanged in Appendix G.3 and Tables 7–9.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain identical splits, normalization, look-back lengths, forecast horizons, MSE/MAE metrics, optimization settings, early stopping, and efficiency-measurement procedures.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Tables 2–3 and 10–11, synthetic mask study in Figure 8, and reconstruction, mask-evolution, and SNR analyses in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the multiple-random-seed SNR experiments and Figure 18 boxplots in Appendix E.3. The benchmark tables still omit error bars, and the run, seed, and uncertainty disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All tabulated and plotted results match, including Appendix H. For example, Table 1 reports ETTh1 MSE of 0.457 for CycleNet and 0.431 for CycleNet with the proposal in both versions. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Section 2.1's definition and hypothesis, Section 3's loss derivations, and Appendix C's gradient-constraint and spectral-normalization reasoning are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about self-supervised relabeling, improved generalization across forecasting backbones, and avoiding additional inference cost.

C2.justification: The overfitting explanations, multiple-instance-learning analogy, channel-alignment interpretation, and baseline-reproduction qualifications are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same architectural scope and lack of LLM-scale testing.

D1.justification: Appendices D and G retain identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and training-efficiency information. Code and data access disclosures are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix F, and the 54-entry bibliography are identical. No cited work, novelty statement, or relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes affiliation markers for Dalin Zhang from 2 to 3, Yuxuan Liang from 3 to 4, Hua Lu from 4 to 5, and Gang Chen from 1 to 1,2. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–11 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the title-page differences are confined to metadata text.

improvement.justification: v4 only updates author-affiliation markers and the arXiv version/date information. The scientific argument, experiments, appendix evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation are unchanged, supporting no meaningful overall quality difference.
